questions.q: What is a DAG, as distinct from a DAG Run?
options: The pipeline's definition — a Python file that doesn't run by itself
One specific execution tied to a logical date
A single task within one execution
A synonym for Task Instance
questions.explain: A DAG is the template/definition; a DAG Run is one specific execution of that definition.

options: One specific task, within one specific DAG Run
The entire DAG definition file
A synonym for a DAG Run
A type of Operator
questions.explain: The same task has a different Task Instance for every DAG Run it's been part of — it's task + run, together.

questions.q: What does 'Try Number' show in a Task Instances table?
options: How many times this specific Task Instance has been attempted
The total number of tasks in the DAG
How many DAG Runs exist for this DAG
The task's priority level
questions.explain: Try Number tracks attempts for that specific instance — a value greater than 1 means a retry actually fired.

questions.q: What does an 'Upstream Failed' state mean, as distinct from 'Failed'?
options: The task never ran at all because a dependency failed first
The task ran and crashed with an error
The task succeeded but slowly
There is no difference — they mean the same thing
questions.explain: Upstream Failed means the task was correctly skipped because something it depends on failed — it was never actually attempted.

questions.q: Why is 'the task failed' an incomplete sentence, according to this lesson?
options: Because it doesn't say which specific run — the task's definition didn't change, one instance of it did
Because tasks can never actually fail in Airflow
Because only DAGs can fail, not individual tasks
Because failure states don't exist in Airflow
questions.explain: A task can succeed on one run and fail on another — without naming the run, the statement is ambiguous.
